stem: Anil faces South. He turns 180 degrees. He then turns 90 degrees clockwise. Which direction does he now face?

per_option_rationale.rationale: South + 180 degrees = North. From North, 90 degrees clockwise (N->E) = East.
West results from taking a 90-degree anticlockwise turn from North, confusing the direction of rotation.
North is the position after the 180-degree turn only; the second 90-degree clockwise turn was not applied.
South is the starting position; failing to apply both turns gives the wrong answer.

explanation: Starting from South: a 180-degree turn faces North. From North, a 90-degree clockwise turn (N->E) faces East. Two sequential turns must both be applied.

explanation_sections.punchline: 180 degrees from South reaches North; one more clockwise quarter-turn from North reaches East.
explanation_sections.approach: Deductive trace: apply turns one at a time. Clockwise order is N->E->S->W. South + 180 = North (two clockwise steps). North + 90 CW = East (one clockwise step). Final answer: East.
explanation_sections.lesson: Apply each turn in sequence, tracking the current heading; do not skip any step or mix up clockwise and anticlockwise.
explanation_sections.timing: 20-30 seconds. The main traps are stopping after the first turn (gives North, option 3) and turning anticlockwise instead of clockwise after the 180 (gives West, option 2).
